text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The High Court awards damages totalling Singapore $8.075 million to 11 People's Action Party leaders who sued Tang Liang Hong for calling them liars and criminals during the General Election in January.

- Ruling party Golkar looks set to coast home to another crushing victory as polls closed quietly amid tight security and reports of pre-election day violence in the troubled province of East Timor, where at least 14 people died.
- Popular Television Corporation of Singapore (TCS) actor Li Nanxing was fined Singapore $4,000 and banned from driving for 30 months for drink driving.

- Former Amcol Holdings' executive director Ng Chee Kheong was sentenced to 18 months' jail for conspiring to cheat the company into investing in a Mauritian resort project at an inflated price of US$39.6 million.

- The latest batch of state plots for private residential development are mostly "average suburban sites" expected to draw fairly measured bids because of the relatively high supply this year, said market observers.
- Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd, the business arm of China's capital city government, rose more than three-fold on the first trading day for the hottest new stock in Hongkong's history.
- The annual growth of regional retirement schemes ranges from 25 percent in Hongkong to 50 percent in Thailand, and these assets could exceed US$200 billion by year 2000, a new survey predicts.
- Keppel Land and the government-owned Health Corporation of Singapore are ending their partnership to set up medical facilities in the region.

- Germany's Hoechst group says it will be building two world-scale primary chemical plants -- which industry officials estimate would cost as much as US$500 million in total -- at Pulau Sakra in Singapore.
- Mainboard-bound Huan Hsin Holdings is offering 50 million new shares at 42 US cents each, with a low historical price-to-earnings ratio of 8.8 times.
- The Land Transport Authority has appointed ICS Insurance as the sole insurer to underwrite risks for the construction of the north-east MRT line.
- Singapore Airlines has to think bigger and be even more brash to become a world airline in the era of open skies, Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong says.
